text.en: Floor tiles are often parallelograms or rectangles. Their shape rules tell us why they fit together without gaps.

A quadrilateral has four sides and four angles, and the sum of its interior angles is 360 degrees.
A parallelogram has both pairs of opposite sides parallel. Its opposite sides are equal and opposite angles are equal.
The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
A rectangle is a parallelogram with all angles 90 degrees and equal diagonals.
A rhombus has four equal sides and its diagonals bisect at right angles.
A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus.
A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides; the mid-point theorem says the segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half of it.

problem.en: In a parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 70 degrees. Find the other angles.

text.en: Opposite angles are equal, so angle C = 70 degrees.
Adjacent angles add to 180 degrees: angle B = 180 - 70 = 110 degrees.

prompt.en: List three properties of a parallelogram and how a rhombus differs.

requiredIdeas.en: Rhombus has equal sides and perpendicular diagonals

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all parallelograms have equal diagonals

points.en: Angle sum of a quadrilateral is 360 degrees.
Parallelogram: opposite sides/angles equal; diagonals bisect each other.
Rhombus: four equal sides; diagonals at right angles.
Mid-point theorem: segment = half of the third side.
